result.summary: The pedestrian environment features wide sidewalks and a signalized intersection with marked crosswalks. However, the large intersection footprint results in long crossing distances and potentially high vehicle turning speeds due to the wide corner radii.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide intersection requires pedestrians to spend significant time in the roadway, increasing exposure to vehicles.

hazards.name: Large corner radius
hazards.description: The wide curve at the corner allows vehicles to make right turns at higher speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace standard parallel line markings with continental or ladder style markings for better visibility.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, curb ramps, and traffic signals. However, the environment is characterized by a wide crossing distance and a lack of visible pavement markings, which increases pedestrian exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Missing Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The absence of high-visibility crosswalk markings at a signalized intersection reduces driver awareness of pedestrian crossing zones.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide expanse of the intersection increases the time pedestrians are exposed to potential vehicle conflicts without a refuge.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and uneven road surfaces can create tripping hazards or difficulties for users with mobility devices.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style high-visibility crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver yielding.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to provide a 3-7 second head start for pedestrians before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The environment features basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks, curb ramps with tactile warnings, and continuous sidewalks. However, the wide intersection geometry and proximity of parked vehicles to the crossing area create potential visibility and speed-related risks.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large black truck is parked very close to the intersection corner, potentially obscuring pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, parked near the corner of the intersection.

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry appears wide, which can encourage higher vehicle speeds during right-hand turns across the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground right, where the sidewalk meets the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extension (Bulb-out)
interventions.description: Install a curb extension to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles by tightening the corner radius.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked crosswalk and a well-maintained sidewalk with curb ramps. However, the lack of pedestrian signals and the presence of parked cars near the crossing create visibility and safety concerns for those crossing the street.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk on both sides of the street obstruct the sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both the left and right sides of the street leading up to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Unsignalized Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks a pedestrian signal or stop control for vehicles, requiring pedestrians to judge gaps in traffic on a multi-lane one-way street.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection in the foreground.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they step into the travel lane.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.
